name: Jenkins
author: Smart Terminal
summary: Your Jenkins as a tree you can read at a glance — what is broken, what is running, and a build's log that follows itself.
description: Every job on your Jenkins, browsable as two trees you switch between: Tree, which is how the jobs are organised — folders, jobs and their latest builds — and Views, which is how you and your team group them: the smart ones that are worked out live (failing, running, unstable, stale, disabled) and the views Jenkins itself has, nested ones included. Each node carries its status, so you can see where the red is without opening anything, and a search box reaches any job on the server by name. The Dashboard answers the one question people open Jenkins to ask — what needs me, what is running, and how has it been going — with the failing jobs and anything stuck or waiting for an answer on top, then what is running now, the builds of the last hour, day, week or month on a timeline you can zoom and travel in, and how load, failures and build times have moved. A job shows its parameters as a form that remembers what you typed last time, and a plain Run when it has none. A build shows its stages, what changed, and its console, which follows itself while the build is still writing and can jump to the first error. Everything that changes arrives by itself: the app watches the server from one place and tells the panel only what is different, so nothing here polls and a build you asked to follow still ends in a notification with the panel closed. Ask Claude opens a session that has already been handed the failed build — its stages, its changes and the end of its log. The server's address, your user and an API token are kept by the app, encrypted; this panel never holds the token and cannot reach the network at all.

panels.summary: Jobs, builds and logs — and a Claude session aimed at the one that failed.
